title: Fullness of the discrete representation to internal group functor
statement: For every topological group $G$ and carrier universe $w$, equip $\mathcal C=\mathrm{DiscreteContAction}(\mathrm{Type}(w),G)$ with a Cartesian monoidal structure and braiding. The functor $H$ of [def-exc-discrete-continuous-rep-to-commgrp] is full: every internal group morphism $H(M)\to H(N)$ is induced by an equivariant integer-linear map $M\to N$.

proof.text: For every pair of equivariant maps s,t from X to the underlying action of M, multiplication in Hom(X,H(M)) evaluates pointwise as s(x)+t(x). This follows by evaluating the represented multiplication after the Cartesian lift, and using lift_fst and lift_snd.

Form the product representation M×M. Its stabilizer at (x,y) is the intersection of the open stabilizers of x and y. Apply the internal group morphism to the product of the two projection maps, and evaluate at (x,y). Thus its underlying equivariant function preserves addition.

Preservation of addition implies preservation of zero by cancellation. Use int_smul_eq_zsmul for each stored module structure and map_zsmul for the additive homomorphism to obtain integer-linearity. Equivariance is already part of the underlying action morphism. The resulting representation morphism maps to the original internal morphism since their underlying functions coincide.

proof_origin.note: Explicit categorical and elementwise expansion of the formal identification in the source.
